method: Rule-based intersection scoring using paper coverage in primary and secondary taxonomy bins. Scores indicate underrepresentation in this local index, not verified novelty.

opportunities.title: Contact-Calibrated World-Action Models with Tactile Counterfactuals
opportunities.problem: Video-centric WAMs can predict visually plausible futures while missing contact, friction, slip and force transitions. This makes imagined outcomes unreliable precisely when manipulation becomes contact-rich.
opportunities.hypothesis: A compact tactile-conditioned latent transition model, trained alongside visual future prediction, can detect when a candidate action is likely to produce an unsafe or unsuccessful contact state before execution.
opportunities.minimal_experiment: Start with a single-arm peg insertion or object sliding task in Isaac Lab/MuJoCo. Train a visual-only latent world model and a vision+tactile variant. Predict short-horizon end-effector/object state and slip/contact events; evaluate action selection under friction, mass and viewpoint shifts. Add a small real tactile validation set only after simulation baselines are stable.
resources: LIBERO/ManiSkill or a custom insertion benchmark
A low-cost tactile sensor or GelSight-like sensor for later validation
opportunities.risks: Simulation tactile mismatch, incomplete contact labels, and extra sensor latency. Keep the initial claim to short-horizon contact prediction rather than general physical reasoning.
opportunities.novelty_caveat: Vision-tactile policies and tactile world models already exist. Novelty must be established specifically for counterfactual, action-conditioned tactile prediction coupled to WAM candidate selection.
opportunities.deliverable: A reproducible benchmark and a contact-aware WAM ablation showing when tactile prediction changes the selected action.

opportunities.title: Uncertainty-Gated Failure Recovery for Frozen VLAs
opportunities.problem: Failure detectors can identify risky trajectories, and correction methods can learn interventions, but they are often separate components. A robot needs to decide when to continue, observe again, ask for help or execute a correction.
opportunities.hypothesis: A calibrated latent uncertainty monitor can gate a small library of corrective skills, and only invoke expensive VLM/WAM deliberation when confidence is low or failure probability crosses a calibrated threshold.
opportunities.minimal_experiment: Use a frozen OpenVLA/Octo checkpoint on LIBERO-Plus. Inject controlled perturbations (object pose, camera, distractors, gripper slip proxies). Train a lightweight failure predictor on latent states; compare fixed-threshold, calibrated and uncertainty-conditioned recovery. Measure success, false interventions, recovery time and inference overhead.
opportunities.risks: False positives may interrupt successful actions; synthetic failures may not match real failures. Separate detection, diagnosis and recovery metrics.
opportunities.novelty_caveat: Runtime failure prediction and VLA recovery are active topics. A defensible contribution needs a new calibrated decision policy and careful real-time cost/benefit evaluation, not simply another failure classifier.
opportunities.deliverable: An open evaluation harness with calibrated early-warning metrics and a selective-recovery baseline.

opportunities.title: Human Video to Robot-Ready 3D Interaction Graphs
opportunities.problem: Human video offers abundant interaction examples but lacks robot-coordinate actions. 2D motion transfer alone often loses object geometry, contact state and embodiment constraints.
opportunities.hypothesis: A pipeline that converts egocentric clips into object-centric 3D interaction graphs (object, contact region, relative motion, inferred affordance) can provide an embodiment-neutral intermediate representation for downstream robot policy learning.
opportunities.minimal_experiment: Select 2–3 tasks such as opening a drawer, placing an object and tool use. Extract object tracks and hand-object contacts from public videos, estimate relative 3D geometry where available, encode interaction graphs, then retarget graph constraints to a simulated Franka or bimanual arm. Compare against 2D keypoint retargeting and direct video-conditioned imitation.
resources: Ego4D or other licensed egocentric video
SAM 2 / object tracking and hand pose tools
Open X-Embodiment / DROID as robot-side data
opportunities.risks: Depth ambiguity, occlusion, and inaccurate inferred contact can corrupt the graph. Explicitly report confidence and abstain from retargeting uncertain segments.
opportunities.novelty_caveat: Human-video action discovery and 3D interaction reasoning are established. Novelty could lie in the graph as a transferable, measurable interface between human demonstrations and robot action policies.
opportunities.deliverable: A small open dataset of interaction graphs plus cross-embodiment retargeting baselines.

opportunities.title: Latency-Aware Predictive Feature Scheduling for WAMs
opportunities.problem: A WAM may have strong predictive representations but still miss control deadlines because perception, future feature extraction, action generation and safety checks execute serially or contend for memory bandwidth.
opportunities.hypothesis: An asynchronous scheduler can allocate compute to predictive features only when they change the chosen action, using confidence and deadline-aware early exits to reduce tail latency without materially reducing task success.
opportunities.minimal_experiment: Instrument a compact WAM and a VLA baseline. Profile encoder, prediction head, action head, safety monitor and data movement. Implement asynchronous queues and an adaptive predictive horizon. Compare p50/p95/p99 latency, deadline misses, memory, energy and closed-loop success on one GPU and one edge device.
resources: A compact JEPA-style or latent WAM baseline
LIBERO-Plus and a real-time control loop
opportunities.risks: Asynchronous execution may create stale observations or mismatched action horizons. Correctness requires timestamped observations and explicit action cancellation semantics.
opportunities.novelty_caveat: Inference acceleration and asynchronous robot control are mature topics. Novelty must be specific to predictive-feature scheduling and demonstrate a measurable closed-loop advantage over standard kernel and batching optimizations.
opportunities.deliverable: A profiling suite and scheduler that trades prediction depth against action deadlines with reproducible latency/success curves.

opportunities.title: Counterfactual Safety Audits for Action-Conditioned World Models
opportunities.problem: World-model benchmarks often emphasize prediction quality or downstream success, but can miss whether the model correctly distinguishes safe and unsafe counterfactual actions in the same scene.
opportunities.hypothesis: A paired counterfactual benchmark can expose action-insensitive or physically inconsistent world models by comparing predictions for near-identical scenes under safe and unsafe interventions.
opportunities.minimal_experiment: Build 8–10 controlled manipulation scenarios with paired actions that differ in force, approach direction or timing. Record physical outcomes in simulation, test video/latent world models on future state, collision, contact and task completion, then measure whether action ranking matches actual outcomes under distribution shift.
resources: DINO/JEPA latent predictors and one video WAM baseline
Metrics for pairwise ranking, calibration and physical violation
opportunities.risks: Simulator ground truth may reward simulator-specific cues. Include randomized physics and, where possible, a small physical validation suite.
opportunities.novelty_caveat: Counterfactual evaluation and action-conditioned prediction are known. The contribution would be a carefully controlled benchmark isolating action sensitivity and safety ranking, with simulator integrity checks.
opportunities.deliverable: A benchmark that scores counterfactual action ranking, physical consistency and calibration rather than video similarity alone.

opportunities.title: Privacy-Preserving Continual Adaptation from On-Robot Interaction
opportunities.problem: Robots collect sensitive household and workplace observations. Continual adaptation risks retaining identifiable visual information or leaking past interaction examples.
opportunities.hypothesis: A replay-light adaptation pipeline using privacy-filtered latent summaries, selective gradient updates and membership-risk auditing can improve task performance without retaining raw video indefinitely.
opportunities.minimal_experiment: Fine-tune a small policy adapter on a sequence of simulated tasks and user-like scenes. Compare raw replay, feature replay and DP/noised adapter updates. Measure retention, forgetting, task success, privacy attack success and inference overhead.
opportunities.risks: Privacy mechanisms can reduce utility; feature summaries may still encode sensitive information. Threat model and privacy accountant must be explicit.
opportunities.novelty_caveat: DP fine-tuning and continual learning are established. A contribution must tie privacy guarantees and empirical leakage audits to embodied continual adaptation, including the sensor pipeline.
opportunities.deliverable: A reproducible privacy–utility benchmark for sequential VLA adaptation.
